judge_reasoning: All candidates aim to answer “Give radius for observable universe.” Candidate [1] gives a widely used estimate (~46.5 billion light-years, ~4.4×10^26 meters) consistent with the standard particle-horizon radius; it directly matches the requested quantity and units. Candidate [2] shows an incorrect derivation and lands at 64.7 billion light-years, which is substantially off. Candidates [3] and [4] compute radii by incorrect/insufficient cosmological reasoning and also produce values that are off by large factors (especially [4], which is orders of magnitude too small).
